target.title: fix(logging): redact Telegram bot tokens from timeout URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a fetch to the Telegram Bot API times out, the diagnostic log URL produced by `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl` exposes the bot token in the path segment (`/bot<TOKEN>/...`). While the function strips userinfo, query, and hash, it did not redact credential-bearing path segments. 

The original fix only covered `api.telegram.org`, but Telegram supports custom self-hosted/proxy `apiRoot` values — the `probeTelegram` path builds `${apiBase}/bot${token}/getMe`, so a timeout from `https://telegram.internal/bot123456:.../getMe` would still leak the token even after the initial fix.

Fixes #96982

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a purpose-built `redactBotTokenPath` function that uses a strict regex requiring ≥6-digit bot ID + colon or `%3A` + ≥20-character secret. The regex is strict enough to avoid false positives on ordinary `/bot/settings`-style routes.

**Revision 2**: Moved the Telegram bot token redactor from a hostname-gated registry (`api.telegram.org` only) to a **universal** redactor list applied to all URLs regardless of hostname. This covers custom self-hosted Telegram API roots and proxy roots. The hostname registry is preserved for future extensibility.

## User Impact

All users running Telegram plugin will no longer have their bot tokens logged in plaintext when fetch timeouts occur — including users with custom `apiRoot` configurations. The token is replaced with `/bot***` in timeout log messages. Non-Telegram bot paths are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
- `pnpm test packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/utils/fetch-timeout.test.ts` — 50/50 passed (31 net-policy + 19 fetch-timeout)
- New tests: custom self-hosted API root redaction, proxy API root redaction, any-hostname redaction
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint ...` — clean
- `pnpm format:check ...` — All matched files use the correct format

### Real Gateway Proof (no-proxy environment → Telegram API unreachable → timeout triggered)

Gateway started without proxy env vars, Telegram channel enabled. The probe to `api.telegram.org/bot***/getMe` timed out as expected:

```
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 14997ms (elapsed 14998ms) operation=fetchWithTimeout url=https://api.telegram.org/bot***/getMe
```

The actual bot token was completely absent from the log output — verified with `grep` for the known token value.

Full gateway log preserved at `/tmp/gateway-telegram-proof.log`.

**Environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, commit `6f63ee4bab`, no proxy (env cleared: `http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `all_proxy`, `no_proxy`).

Behavior addressed: Telegram bot tokens in timeout log URLs are now redacted to `/bot***` for all hostnames, including custom/proxy API roots.
Real environment tested: Gateway startup without proxy — Telegram probe fetched `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getMe`, connection timed out, and the timeout log showed `url=https://api.telegram.org/bot***/getMe` with the token fully redacted.
Evidence after fix: 50/50 tests pass, gateway timeout log shows `bot***`, lint/format clean.
Observed result after fix: Bot tokens in `/bot<TOKEN>/...` paths are replaced with `/bot***` in `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl` output for all hostnames.
What was not tested: No custom `apiRoot` live environment available — custom API root coverage is validated through unit tests with `https://telegram.internal/bot<TOKEN>/getMe` and `https://tg-proxy.example.com/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage`.
